design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - task 1 (hardship_hold_requests). frozen_time 2026-10-12 10:20:00 EDT (Monday).

[0] DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 1): {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 5, 4]}. Assignment: hardship_ext_service_review_proof 6, hardship_ext_service_extension 5, hardship_ext_service_documentation 4.

[1] SCOPE SNAPSHOT. Occupied by task 0: the Long-Term Hardship Hold side - cure notice (send_cure_notice_c402292e), long-term extension (extend_longterm_hold_aa9e035f), income records request (request_income_records_8e86e9ce), medical recertification request (request_medical_recertification_c8d32721). Claimed here (disjoint): hardship_ext_service_documentation / request_service_documentation_e72ed459, hardship_ext_service_extension / extend_service_hold_a0a57648 (owner user), hardship_ext_service_review_proof / request_service_review_proof_12b8aafa. After this task all seven extended policies are claimed; nothing is reserved. The Military tier is distinct in rule and evidence: protection rests on the servicemember's orders (so the extension is the servicemember's own election, carrying post-service protection on the last allowed one), reviews run every 90 days with a 30-day overdue window, requests are consumer-level, and a new request on a newly placed account starts with an initial documentation request rather than a cure. Same blueprint constraints as task 0 (no approval write, no term/consumer end write, no request write).

[2] DESIGN THESIS. Surface goal: SFC Okafor-Lindqvist asks for the proof request for his 2026-10-15 status review and its due date. Scored core: due_in_days of the status review proof request (46). Hidden chain: (a) the proof due date is worked out only once the hold's end date lies beyond the review (end 2026-10-14 < review 2026-10-15) -> the servicemember must book his extension himself on the orders mailed 2026-10-01 (256 days); (b) the proof request is not sent until every undecided Military request of his carries its initial documentation request -> the Cape Fear request recorded 2026-10-02 has none -> initial documentation request (37 days). Depth: proof <- extension (value hop) and proof <- documentation request (state hop). Breadth: hold history (reviews, extensions, channels), account records (stage, validation period, term length, contact restriction, payments, placements).

[3] PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
 root hardship_ext_service_review_proof (agent).
 edge E1 root -> hardship_ext_service_extension: value_input, gate sv_end_room, form state, sentence "Before the status review proof due date is worked out, the hold's end date on record must already lie beyond that review's due date." (affirmative direction, 'before ... must'). Opening falsity: 2a869859-de15-4049-9e1d-3d1b665619c5 end_date 2026-10-14, start 2025-10-20, review due 2026-10-15. Only an extension moves a Military hold's end date, and for this tier the extension write is the servicemember's (extend_service_hold_a0a57648, owner user). Deletion run: proof 46 -> 2.
 edge E2 root -> hardship_ext_service_documentation: state_gate, gate hardship_hold_events.event_type, form state, sentence "The status review proof request is not sent until every undecided Military Service Hold request of the servicemember carries its initial documentation request, so that one set of orders answers all of them." (negated direction: a request release 'is not sent until'). Opening falsity: a4d301e6-a8bf-413d-a9f6-f2a32f37173f status requested, request 2026-10-02, no history rows at all. Only the initial documentation write records a first documentation request on an undecided Military request (a cure needs a prior submission; review requests concern running holds). Deletion run: proof value unchanged (46) but the Cape Fear request row due 2026-11-18 is missing from the terminal state.
 Four-point test passed for both (connective, record-visible state, no tool/id/code token, scope 'every undecided Military request of the servicemember' / 'end date beyond that review').
 Topological order: documentation request, extension, review proof; the first two commute (replay hash identical when swapped). value_input edges: 1 >= max(2-1,1).
 user_scenario names no prerequisite; the orders and the Cape Fear request are facts given only on questions; the extension and documentation request appear only in reactions to the agent's own statements. Tools validate nothing.

[4] FACTOR CARD (tier / evidence / result with that factor at baseline).
 hardship_ext_service_documentation (baseline 20 = 30 days after the 2026-10-02 request; gold 37):
  in_send_anchor (method): letter 10 days after the request (> 7) -> 30 days from sending -> 27.
  in_validation (parameter, cross account; both tier-1 conditions read the same account row, so not counted as multi-source): Cape Fear validation_period until 2026-10-30 -> 5 -> 32. Near-miss: the card account's validation period ended 2025-09-19.
  in_term_length (parameter, cross account, CPARAM): Early-Out term 150 -> cut 5 -> 42.
  in_contact_route (parameter, cross account): no-email restriction 2025-11-03 -> 7 -> 30.
 hardship_ext_service_extension (baseline 180; gold 256):
  sx_review_anchor (method, multi-source): review 2026-10-15 one day after the end, 3/3 reviews continued -> +31 -> 225.
  sx_carry (parameter): 1 of 3 extensions recorded -> one further remains -> 15 -> 241.
  sx_stage_protection (parameter, cross account): Legal Review Placement -> 30 -> 226.
  sx_payment_cut (parameter, cross account): net 100.00 dated less than six whole months before today -> cut 15 -> 271.
  sx_new_placement (parameter, cross account): one placement less than two whole months before today (Cape Fear 2026-09-21) -> 15 -> 241.
 hardship_ext_service_review_proof (baseline 33 = 3 + 30; gold 46):
  sv_count_point (method): review 3 days away (<= 7) -> 30 from the request -> 49.
  sv_proof_mailing (parameter, multi-source): fax + mail and 4 electronic submissions -> mixed 5 -> 41.
  sv_extension_history (parameter): 2 extensions after the servicemember's booking -> 10 -> 36.
  sv_review_record (parameter, multi-source): 3/3 continued, >= 3 -> 7 -> 39.
  sv_stage_cut (parameter, cross account): Legal Review -> cut 10 -> 56.
  sv_new_placement (parameter, cross account): one recent placement -> 4 -> 42.
 Every factor moves its result; all-baseline figures 20 / 180 / 33 differ from gold. Overrides declared: initial documentation due date and documentation period (hardship_evt_documentation), days per extension (hardship_evt_extension). Inherited unchanged: documentation channels, review interval/overdue, maximum extensions, window, active and before-end gates, consumer-level request semantics, hold-day limit (Military days do not count).

[5] BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Documentation requests: hardship_evt_documentation only, gate applies to denials -> policy_scope. Extension: extension_on_active_hold (2a869859-de15-4049-9e1d-3d1b665619c5 active); extension_before_end - start 2025-10-20 + 180 + 1 x 180 - 1 = 2026-10-14, not_after, inclusive: 2026-10-12 passes, 2026-10-14 passes, 2026-10-15 fails. Window 30 days before end (from 2026-09-14) open; updated orders on record (2026-10-01); 1 of 3 extensions used.

[6] BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Proof request and extension: object 2a869859-de15-4049-9e1d-3d1b665619c5; evidence = its history, the card account's stage and payments, the consumer's placements. Initial documentation: object a4d301e6-a8bf-413d-a9f6-f2a32f37173f; evidence = its request date, the Cape Fear account's status/validation end/stage, the consumer's contact restrictions. Excluded: the card account's own placement (outside the two-month window), the card account's validation period (not the requested account).

[7] SEED ROWS AND WHY. Consumer; card account (Legal Review, hardship_hold) with placement and two 50.00 payments (payment cut); Cape Fear account (Early-Out, validation_period) with its placement (new-placement allowances, validation allowance, term cut); one no-email restriction (contact route); running Military hold + 18 history rows (initial request/submission, decision letter, client notifications, three review cycles, extension 1 with its orders, end notice, new orders by mail) feeding anchor, carry, channels, extension history and review record; undecided Cape Fear request with no history (the unmet state). Automatic clauses: hold inside its term (end 2026-10-14 ahead), reviews on time, Cape Fear request inside its documentation period, client notified for approval and extension.

[8] PERSONA. Clipped, date-minded NCO; volunteers only the review proof request for October 15; identity on request (phone 9105554263, SSN last four 4729, DOB/ZIP extra); on questions mentions the Cape Fear account, his 2026-10-02 call and the orders mailed in October; reacts to the documentation request and the extension hand-over only after the agent explains them; re-check only on the agent's own contradiction; closes after hearing the proof due date. No ask of his own beyond the root.

[9] CAPABILITY CARDS. extend_service_hold_a0a57648 (owner user): one extension row + hold end_date/extension_count update; receipt extension_ref, hold_id, extension_number, days_added, previous_end_date, new_end_date, status. request_service_review_proof_12b8aafa / request_service_documentation_e72ed459 (owner agent): one active-duty proof request row due today + days on a running hold / an undecided request; receipt request_ref, hold_id, document_type, due_date, sent_on, status. No checks, no errors, date maths via the class helper.

[10] REACHABILITY WALK. Locate by phone, verify with phone + SSN last four, read accounts, holds, both hold histories, money history and case history. The proof rule shows two waits: the Cape Fear request lacks its initial documentation request (record it: 37 days, 2026-11-18) and the end date does not reach the review (the extension rule makes it his own booking: hand over hold reference + 256 days; he reads back new end 2027-06-27). Then record the proof request (46 days, 2026-11-27) and tell him; he repeats it and hangs up. One frozen time, no real-world waits.

[11] EASY MISTAKES. Proof before the extension (2); counting the card account's 2025 placement as recent; using the card account's validation period or term for the Cape Fear request; forgetting the extension already granted when counting extensions left (carry 0 or 90 instead of 15); anchoring the initial documentation on the request date (20).

[12] VERIFICATION. Authoring script replayed gold with the real tools and evaluated computes with check_compute's evaluator: 37 / 256 / 46; baselines 20 / 180 / 33; per-factor figures as in [4]; skip runs as in [3]. Gates (--task 1): EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK (closure 28 = seed 28), SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK (factors 15, cross 8, history 15, branches 43, steps 14), GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK.

[13] CLOSURE. service_documentation -> request_service_documentation_e72ed459 -> step 9 due_in_days 37 -> Cape Fear request row due 2026-11-18; service_extension -> extend_service_hold_a0a57648 -> step 11 extension_days 256 -> end 2027-06-27, extension #2; service_review_proof -> request_service_review_proof_12b8aafa -> step 13 due_in_days 46 -> proof request due 2026-11-27. Scope = required_documents = these three, tools in first-call order. Difficulty-wide: tasks 0 and 1 together cover all seven extended policies with disjoint scopes.

[14] DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT: the published rules plus finder returns give the same three writes, order constraints and figures; the only order freedom (documentation request vs extension) commutes.


[15] REWORK ROUND 2 (policy-task audit r1). Task 1 passed; its scored values are unchanged: 37 / 256 / 46, baselines 20 / 180 / 33, every per-factor figure unchanged, same writes and order.
 CG-1: the service extension (payment cut, new placements) and review proof (new placements) rules now state the windows as 'less than N whole months before today, whole months being the difference in calendar months between the date and today, less one when today's day of the month is smaller than the date's day of the month' (the within_months semantics); no row of this world lies in the divergence band.
 CG-2 / O-7: the service extension declares the current end date as the end date on record (overwrites on hardship_evt_extension and hardship_evt_end) and the servicemember's booking as the decision; before the booking the record (2026-10-14) equals the base formula because extension 1 added the tier's 180 days.
 O-2: both middle tiers that use the tier's decision days now say they are counted as calendar days (neither tier is taken here).
 O-8: the initial documentation request's documentation period now runs to the due date it sets in every case (round 3: unless a cure notice later stands on the request, then to the cure due date).
 O-10: next-review convention stated for the review proof.
 T1-O2: in_validation is no longer labelled multi-source; the task's multi-source factors remain sx_review_anchor, sv_review_record and sv_proof_mailing.
 Gates re-run after the rework: see worklog.md.


[16] REWORK ROUND 3 (policy-task audit revision 2; task 1 passed and is not regressed). Values unchanged: 37 / 256 / 46; baselines 20 / 180 / 33; per-factor 27/32/42/30, 225/241/226/271/241, 49/41/36/39/56/42; same writes, order and terminal state.
 N-1: the initial documentation request's period now defers to a later cure notice, matching the cure policy. In this world the Cape Fear request has no submission, so no cure notice is owed and the period runs to the 37-day due date (2026-11-18).
 N-O2: as in task 0 - the base counting_rule fields repeat sentences the service extension already supersedes; before the booking the record end date 2026-10-14 equals the base formula because extension 1 added the tier's 180 days.
 N-O3: the month windows of the service extension and review proof are now defined arithmetically; the 2026-06-05 and 2026-08-05 payments stay inside six whole months, the 2026-09-21 placement inside two, the 2025-08-11 placement outside.
 Skip runs re-checked by replay: skip extension -> proof 2; skip documentation request -> proof 46.


[17] REWORK ROUND 4 (render-layer audits; task 1 PASS, not regressed). Values unchanged: 37 / 256 / 46; baselines 20 / 180 / 33; per-factor figures unchanged; no rule, overwrite, prerequisite sentence or tool docstring changed. The only charter change is the cure notice's compute (original request = the one dated the request date), which task 1 does not claim; the Cape Fear request has no submission, so no cure notice is owed here. Overwrite-scope, retired-counting-rule and spouse items recorded in worklog.md (the overwrite-scope reason was replaced in round 5 [18] by a charter change); in this world the record end date 2026-10-14 equals the base formula before the booking and the documentation period runs to the 37-day due date.


[18] REWORK ROUND 5 (policy-task audit revision 4; task 1 PASS, not regressed). Values unchanged: 37 / 256 / 46; baselines 20 / 180 / 33; per-factor figures unchanged; no compute, factor, parameter, prerequisite sentence or tool changed.
 R4-F1: the service extension's replacements keep the Military rule and add the handling for every other tier (Long-Term under its own rule; other tiers by the tier's extension days at the consumer's request, decided within the tier's extension decision days; current end date = end date on record for every tier). The service documentation's replacements keep the Military rule and restate, for every other tier, the request-date ask, the tier's documentation days and channels, and the period counted from the day after the request date; once a cure notice stands, the period runs to the cure due date. In this world: Cape Fear request due 2026-11-18 (37 days) with its period running to that date; card hold end date on record 2026-10-14 before the booking (= base formula), booking is the decision - all unchanged.
 R4-O1: concerns cure notices, not claimed by task 1; the Cape Fear request has no submission.
user_scenario:
You are Sergeant First Class Thaddeus Okafor-Lindqvist, forty, an Army logistics NCO stationed at Fort Bragg, calling Ridgeline on your lunch break. You are polite, clipped and a bit impatient, the way you talk to any orderly room, and you like answers in dates. Ridgeline has had your Sandhills card account on military protection since last October. The paperwork you got says your next status review is due on October 15, and you want to get ahead of it: you are calling to have Ridgeline send you the request for the proof it needs for that review and to tell you exactly when that proof is due. You say that at the start, in a sentence or two.

Give identity details only as they are asked for. To be found, you give your phone number, 9105554263. To verify, you give the last four of your Social Security number, 4729; if one more detail is needed you give your date of birth, February 17, 1986 (1986-02-17), or your ZIP code, 28314. Your email is thaddeus.okafor.lindqvist@outlook.com if anyone asks, though you remind them you asked Ridgeline not to email you. You do not carry any Ridgeline reference numbers and tell the agent to look them up. Only if the agent asks about other accounts or recent paperwork do you mention that a Cape Fear Wireless bill was sent over to Ridgeline last month and that you phoned on October 2 to ask for the same military protection on it, and that you mailed in your newest orders, number ORDERS 4426-B-2026, at the start of October. You do not know balances or dates beyond that and leave them to the records. You know nothing about Ridgeline's internal rules and never suggest what should happen first.

You are fine with Ridgeline sending you whatever requests and letters go with your military protection by mail; you only want to hear what was sent and when each thing is due. If the agent tells you the Cape Fear request still needs its documentation request and that it is being sent, you say good, send it, and note the due date. If the agent explains that your protection on the card account has to be extended first and that the extension is something you book yourself in the portal on the orders you already sent, you agree to extend it; when the agent hands it over you book it with exactly the hold reference and number of days the agent gives you, and read back what the portal confirms. If something the agent quotes contradicts what the agent said a moment earlier, you ask them to check the records, but you never offer a number of your own.

When the agent tells you the review proof request has gone out and gives you its due date, you repeat the date, say thanks, and hang up; you have nothing else to raise.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.hold_id: Value a4d301e6-a8bf-413d-a9f6-f2a32f37173f. Basis: 'The initial documentation request is owed on every undecided Military Service Hold request whose history shows no documentation request yet' and the docstring 'the hold reference number of the undecided Military Service Hold request, read from the hardship hold lookup'. Uniqueness: of the two holds, only the Cape Fear request is undecided (status requested) and its history is empty; the card hold is active with its documentation on record since 2025-10-22.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.due_in_days: Value 37. Computed: send anchor 30 (letter 10 days after the 2026-10-02 request, more than 7 -> 30 days after sending) + validation-open 5 (Cape Fear account in validation period until 2026-10-30) - short-term cut 5 (Early-Out term 150 days) + mail-only 7 (no-email restriction 2025-11-03) = 37; due 2026-11-18.

Basis: 'A running Military Service Hold may be extended up to the tier's maximum number of extensions' and the docstring 'the hold reference number of the servicemember's running Military Service Hold, which the agent reads from the hardship hold lookup and gives to the servicemember'. Uniqueness: the only active Military Service Hold; the agent tells it to the servicemember, who copies it.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.extension_days: Value 256. Computed: tier extension days 180 + anchor 31 (next review 2026-10-15 one day after the 2026-10-14 end, three reviews fallen due and continued -> 1 + 30) + penultimate carry 15 (one extension recorded of three, one further remains) + legal protection 30 (Legal Review Placement) - part-payer cut 15 (net 100.00 dated less than six whole months before today) + one-placement days 15 (Cape Fear placed 2026-09-21) = 256; the agent tells the servicemember this figure.

edges.policy_source: Before the status review proof due date is worked out, the hold's end date on record must already lie beyond that review's due date.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The initial documentation request writes only on the Cape Fear request and no computation of the running hold reads that request's rows; the extension writes only on the running hold and the initial documentation computation reads only the Cape Fear request's fields and account records. Replaying with the extension before the documentation request leaves the final DB hash and the values 37 / 256 / 46 unchanged (checked). The extension must precede the review proof request (its due date is worked out only once the end date lies beyond the review), and the documentation request must precede it (the proof request is not sent until every undecided Military request carries its initial documentation request).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the extension keeps the end date 2026-10-14: sv_end_room = 2, so the review proof due_in_days changes from 46 to 2, and the hold end date stays 2026-10-14 instead of 2027-06-27.

Skipping the initial documentation request leaves the review proof value at 46 but the Cape Fear request's documentation request row (due 2026-11-18) is missing from the terminal state, and the proof request goes out while its waited-on state does not hold.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario raises only the review proof request for the October 15 review. The new orders and the Cape Fear request are facts given only when the agent asks about other accounts or recent paperwork; the extension and the Cape Fear documentation request appear only in reactions conditioned on the agent's own statements. No policy id or tool name appears.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: request_service_documentation_e72ed459, extend_service_hold_a0a57648 and request_service_review_proof_12b8aafa read the hold row only to copy customer_id/account_id (and the current end date and count for the extension), then create one history row (plus one hold update for the extension) and return a receipt; none checks status, dates, documentation or other holds, and none returns an Error.

request_binding.action_semantics: An undecided Military request has no documentation request; the initial documentation request is owed on it and is the state the review proof request waits on. It is not a cure notice (nothing was submitted) and not a review request (the request is not running).

base_preconditions.condition: hardship_evt_documentation governs documentation requests and has no gate for this subject; the running Military hold is reviewed every 90 days and continues only on current active-duty proof.

temporal_feasibility.condition: An extension is granted only when the handling date is no later than the hold's current end date counted from its start_date.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: The hold's current end date is start_date plus initial_hold_days plus extension_days for each extension already granted, minus 1, counted in calendar days with the last day included.

boundary_check.just_before: Current end date = 2025-10-20 + 180 + 1 x 180 - 1 = 2026-10-14; on 2026-10-12 (frozen) the handling date is not later than it, so the extension may be granted (window of 30 days open since 2026-09-14).
boundary_check.at_boundary: On 2026-10-14 the extension is still allowed (inclusive); on 2026-10-15 it would be refused and a new request would be needed.
